## Overview
Nuxt frontend for a restaurant reservation application at `host.docker.internal:3002`, proxying `/api/**` to Fastify API on port 3001. Recon is black-box and provisional; runtime routes and assets are attacker-reachable over HTTP.

## Trust Boundaries and Assumptions
Unauthenticated internet/client users can access public booking and static frontend content. Authenticated roles include admin, host, and venueadmin; privileged staff/admin routes should enforce role authorization through proxied API/session. Browser cookies and CORS behavior are relevant. Frontend is not trusted for authorization; API must enforce object ownership and role checks.

## Attack Surface and Attacker Stories
Nuxt pages/routes, static JS bundles/source maps, `/staff/*`, `/admin/*`, host/guest views, public reservation flows, and `/api/**` proxy are in scope. Attackers may enumerate routes/assets, manipulate IDs/codes, submit guest names/notes, and attempt unauthorized staff/admin access. Frontend-only validation, reflected CORS credentials, and unsafe rendering/upload paths would be material if confirmed. Skip `/ingest/**` per scope.

## Severity Calibration
Critical means unauthenticated full auth bypass or broad cross-tenant compromise. High means cross-role privilege escalation, IDOR exposing/modifying sensitive reservations/guests, or stored XSS affecting privileged staff. Medium means authenticated-only authorization gaps, CSRF, or limited data disclosure. Low means metadata, source maps without secrets, or cookie/header hygiene without demonstrated impact.

host.docker.internal:3001.content:
**Overview**
Fastify API for restaurant reservation app, proxied by Nuxt frontend on :3002. Runtime routes are registered from public venue/reservation handlers, staff auth, staff operations, and floor-plan modules. A dev-mode source map/source file exposure on the frontend reveals API source paths but this model focuses API :3001.

**Trust Boundaries and Assumptions**
Unauthenticated internet/client users can access `/public/**`, `/health`, and login. Staff users authenticate via `POST /staff/login`, receiving `gioi_session` HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Lax cookie. Seeded accounts `admin` (super-admin), `host` (venue role host), `venueadmin` (venue role admin), all password `password`; venue slug `bali`. Authorization is intended via session validation, venue access, and admin role checks, with super-admin bypass. Inputs to public reservation, feedback/cancel, query filters, staff mutation bodies, CSV export, floor-plan image/layout are attacker-controlled according to role. CORS defaults to `origin: true, credentials: true` when `CORS_ORIGIN` unset; an onRequest origin deny hook only applies when allowlist configured.

**Attack Surface and Attacker Stories**
Public: `GET /public/venues/:slug`, `GET /public/venues/:slug/availability`, `POST /public/venues/:slug/reservations`, `GET /public/reservations/:code`, `POST /public/reservations/:code/cancel`, `POST /public/reservations/:code/feedback`, `GET /public/venues/:slug/floor-plan`. Auth: `POST /staff/login`, `POST /staff/logout`, `GET /staff/me`. Host/staff: `/staff/day`, `/staff/reservations` (POST), `/staff/reservations/:id` PATCH, status and next-statuses, `/staff/guests` and `:id`. Admin: venue details/update, opening hours, closed dates, venue list/create, users list/create/update/delete, audit-log, analytics, CSV export; floor-plan GET/layout PUT/image PUT. Main realistic stories are unauthenticated access or code guessing on public reservations, cross-venue IDOR, host-to-admin action bypass, mass assignment, stored XSS/CSV formula injection/SVG upload, and CSRF/CORS misuse. Error handler returns structured 4xx and generic 500.

**Severity Calibration**
Critical: authentication bypass or cross-tenant mass data/control. High: cross-venue reservation/guest access or modification, SQL/RCE/SSRF, super-admin escalation. Medium: meaningful CSRF, stored XSS limited to staff, reservation-code disclosure, lower-value IDOR. Low: cookie/header/configuration or enumeration without demonstrated unauthorized impact.
